title: Adoption of structured reporting for abdominal CT: a prospective observational study of use, completeness, time and referrer views
subtitle: First six months after the 2027-01-11 switch, Fenwick Cross Hospital
statement: On 2027-01-11 the department replaces free-text abdominal and pelvic CT reports with a structured template. Whether radiologists use it as intended, whether reports then contain the key elements referrers need for suspected appendicitis, bowel obstruction and cancer staging, whether reporting takes longer, and whether referrers find reports easier to act on are unknown.
whoAffected: Patients having abdominal CT, the radiologists who report about 780 examinations a month, and the surgeons and emergency physicians who act on the reports.
whatHurts: Missing or buried key findings delay decisions, for example on appendicitis or obstruction; a template that is overridden or slows reporting would add cost without benefit.
currentPractice: Free-text reports of variable structure and length.
whyNow: The switch date is fixed, so data collection must be ready before 2027-01-11.
constraints: No extra reporting time for radiologists. Data from the reporting system and a short referrer questionnaire only; no patient contact. One radiology registrar has 3 hours a week for the study from January to July 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Every abdominal CT report tells the treating team what it needs to decide, clearly and without delay.
summary: Problem framed as a prospective observational study of structured reporting adoption.
